# `.well-known/` on dicta.uz

Two app-association files, served as static assets by Cloudflare Pages.
`public/_headers` forces `Content-Type: application/json` on both — the AASA
file is extensionless and would otherwise be served as `octet-stream`, which
silently breaks iOS Universal Links.

## `apple-app-site-association`

**Keep in sync by hand with the app's copy**, which is generated by
`web/app/.well-known/apple-app-site-association/route.ts` and serves
`meet.dicta.uz`. The same links are handed out on both hosts, so both must
claim the same paths.

It claims **only** the shapes `DeepLinkRouter.route(url:)` actually
understands (`ios/Sources/Dicta/DeepLink/DeepLinkRouter.swift`):

| Pattern | Routes to |
| --- | --- |
| `/recap/*` | RecapScreen |
| `/dm/*` | Roundtable (distributed offline) join |
| `/meetings/*` | Meeting Detail sheet |
| `/???-????-???` | Online join code → PreJoin |
| `/????-????` | Roundtable join code → distributed join |

The two code patterns mirror `ONLINE_CODE_RE` / `ROUNDTABLE_CODE_RE` in
`web/lib/join/codeGrammar.ts`. AASA treats `?` as a single-character wildcard,
so the fixed-width grammars express exactly; `caseSensitive: false` lets a link
typed in caps still open the app.

**There is deliberately no `/*` catch-all.** It used to be there behind a list
of excludes, which meant every path on the host was claimed and the exclude
list had to grow with every new page — it never did, so the entire marketing
site (`/download`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/offer`, `/delete-account`, `/ru/*`,
`/en/*`) was being pulled into the app, where nothing matched. Claiming only
what we route means new pages stay in the browser by default instead of by
remembering to exclude them. **Do not add a catch-all back.** In particular
`/app` (the store redirect in `functions/app.js`) must stay unclaimed, or
iPhones with the app installed can never reach the App Store listing.

Adding a new deep link means editing this file, the `route.ts` copy, **and**
`DeepLinkRouter.swift`.

## `assetlinks.json`

Android App Links for `com.norlas.dicta.android`. Two SHA-256 fingerprints: the
upload keystore and the Play App Signing certificate. Both are required — Play
re-signs the uploaded bundle, so the shipped app presents the second one.

Android needs no equivalent tightening: `AndroidManifest.xml` claims specific
paths (`/dm/*` plus a join-code `pathAdvancedPattern`), never a catch-all.

## Verifying

`curl` only proves the files are served and typed correctly:

```
curl -i https://dicta.uz/.well-known/apple-app-site-association
curl -i https://dicta.uz/.well-known/assetlinks.json
```

Whether a link *opens the app* can only be checked on a real device. iOS
fetches the AASA at install time and re-checks daily, so reinstall to force a
refresh.
